subject: R packages using Stan models as backend

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: R packages using Stan models as backend
parts:
Hi!

I am distributing a R package which uses a Stan model to do it's computation in the background (I guess like rstanarm). Right now I am not happy with the way the binary Stan model is packaged. My current approach is to prepare a R/sysdata.rda file before doing a R CMD build on the given platform. The sysdata.rda is setup using devtools and includes a R object which is coming from a stan_model call. With this strategy I can distrubute a binary package which only relies on installation of rstan, but does not force the user to install Rtools which is what I have to avoid.

While this works out, what I do not like about the approach is that this generates a R source package which is platform dependent. That is, the sysdata.rda file must be generated on the target platform already.

Hence, is there a way such that I can dump the C++ translated stan model into the src directory of my package and then use the Stan model as usual? Any recommendations or pointers on this?

Many thanks!

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Re: R packages using Stan models as backend
parts: rstan already generates the C++, but puts it in an R tmp directory (wherever that is for your system) so you could grab the C++ from there.  You'll need to orchestrate the compilation but you could use rstan as a template to figure out how to do that (as reliably as rstan does it).  Another alternative for generating the C++ is to use CmdStan which generates an executable (stanc?) that does this .stan -> .cpp step.  That's the gist of it, but you're probably right that figuring out what rstanarm does is the best way to go first. Krzysztof
